html:
Wrongful death investigation services provide an independent, licensed fact-finding process for attorneys, families, insurers, employers, and other authorized clients after a fatal incident leaves disputed or unanswered questions. The work may involve preserving available evidence, locating witnesses, testing timelines, reviewing records, and coordinating qualified specialists. It does not replace law enforcement, a medical examiner or coroner, an accident investigator, or legal counsel. The first priority is to protect lawful access to information before video, digital records, memories, and physical conditions change.

Wrongful Death Investigation Services: What Should Happen First?

Address immediate safety and reporting obligations first. Call emergency services when appropriate, cooperate with official investigators, and do not enter, move, photograph, collect, or test anything from a restricted scene without lawful authority. A family member, attorney, insurer, or company representative should identify who controls each source of evidence and send preservation requests through the proper legal or business channel.

Create a basic chronology using confirmed facts: when the person was last known safe, when the incident was discovered, who responded, which agencies took jurisdiction, what property or equipment was involved, and where records may exist. Keep original files unchanged. Preserve copies with source, date, time zone, custodian, and method of receipt. The National Institute of Justice warns that evidence can be contaminated or lost when scene work is not methodical.

What Does a Wrongful Death Investigator Do?

A wrongful death investigator develops facts within an agreed scope. Typical tasks include locating and interviewing witnesses, comparing accounts, building an event timeline, identifying cameras and data custodians, researching public records, reviewing supplied photographs and reports, checking entities or contractors, and documenting inconsistencies for follow-up.

The investigator should distinguish verified facts, witness statements, analytical leads, and unresolved conflicts. Scientific opinions belong to the appropriate expert. Cause and manner of death are determined by the legally authorized medicolegal authority, not by a private investigator. The 2024 NIJ death-investigation guide describes the official workflow for scene and body documentation; an independent investigator may review available materials but does not assume that role.

When Should a Private Investigator Be Hired After a Death?

Early involvement can matter when evidence is perishable, but speed must not override authority or compassion. Consider a private investigator for wrongful death when counsel needs additional witness development, a family has specific unresolved factual questions, an insurer requires an independent chronology, or a business must preserve internal records while official inquiries continue.

For traffic evidence, see our accident scene investigation services guide. A private investigator should never interfere with an active official investigation or contact represented parties contrary to counsel's direction.

What Evidence Can an Independent Death Investigation Preserve?

Available sources depend on the incident and lawful access. They may include surveillance video, photographs, 911 and dispatch records, vehicle or equipment data, access logs, maintenance records, training documents, schedules, emails, text messages, social-media material, weather data, maps, receipts, and prior complaints. Medical, personnel, insurance, and device records may require authorization, subpoena, court process, or another lawful basis.

Wrongful death evidence preservation means more than downloading files. Preserve native formats when possible, record the source and collection method, avoid editing originals, calculate file hashes when appropriate, and maintain a clear custody log. For witness work, capture contact information and the witness's own observations before showing other accounts that could influence memory. Our witness location services guide explains that separate process.

Can Private Investigators Investigate Murders?

This is a verified Google autocomplete question. A licensed private investigator may conduct a lawful independent death investigation for an authorized client, including fact development related to a suspected homicide, but cannot exercise police powers or replace the official criminal investigation. The investigator cannot trespass, impersonate law enforcement, obstruct officials, access protected records without authority, or promise a prosecution or outcome.

Potential criminal information should be handled with counsel and the appropriate agency. The objective of private work is a documented, ethical record of available facts—not a competing verdict.

How Do Attorneys Use a Wrongful Death Investigation?

Plaintiff and defense attorneys may use investigators to locate witnesses, authenticate where information came from, test a timeline, identify missing records, inspect publicly accessible locations, perform background research relevant to credibility, or coordinate qualified reconstruction, engineering, digital-forensics, medical, or financial experts. Investigators can also organize exhibits and prepare factual reports for counsel.

The engagement should define who directs the work, confidentiality expectations, deliverables, communication intervals, and whether counsel intends the investigation to assist anticipated litigation. Miami PI Agency does not decide liability, give legal advice, or determine what evidence is admissible. Our litigation support service page outlines related support for legal teams.

What Changes in a Workplace Fatality Investigation?

Workplace deaths can involve overlapping duties for the employer, OSHA or a state-plan agency, law enforcement, insurers, unions, equipment owners, and counsel. OSHA states that an employer must report a work-related fatality within eight hours. A private engagement is not a substitute for that obligation or for preserving the site as directed by authorities.

An investigator may help identify document custodians, interview available witnesses, compare training and maintenance records, trace contractors, and assemble a time-stamped chronology. Counsel should guide privileged work and any contact with employees or represented parties.

How Long Does a Wrongful Death Investigation Take?

There is no universal timeline. Initial preservation and witness triage may begin within hours or days. Records requests, official reports, toxicology, complex reconstruction, digital forensics, multi-state fieldwork, and expert review can take weeks or months.

Ask for phases rather than a prediction: urgent preservation, preliminary timeline, priority interviews, records follow-up, specialist coordination, interim findings, and final reporting. A responsible investigator explains dependencies and limitations without guaranteeing answers.

How Much Do Wrongful Death Investigation Services Cost?

Cost depends on urgency, locations, hours, number of witnesses, travel, records, surveillance or scene work, digital evidence, expert needs, and report requirements. Agencies may bill hourly with a retainer and require written approval before exceeding a budget. Reconstructionists, forensic pathologists, engineers, laboratories, or expert testimony are usually separate expenses.

Request written rates, expense rules, authorization thresholds, communication frequency, deliverables, data-handling practices, and stop conditions.

What Should You Ask Before Hiring a Wrongful Death Investigator?

  • Who will perform the work, and where are they licensed?
  • What experience matches the specific incident type?
  • How will official investigators, counsel, insurers, and experts be kept separate or coordinated?
  • How are original files, notes, metadata, time zones, and custody records preserved?
  • Will reports separate confirmed facts, statements, analysis, limitations, and open questions?
  • Which tasks are urgent, optional, outside scope, or dependent on legal process?

Miami PI Agency is a licensed Florida private investigative agency. Fieldwork outside Florida is performed by investigators licensed in the state where the activity occurs. We do not provide legal advice, determine civil liability, or promise that evidence, witnesses, recovery, settlement, or criminal charges will result. Consult qualified counsel about deadlines, standing, record access, preservation notices, and litigation strategy.

Request a Confidential Case Assessment

Prepare the agency names and case numbers, incident date and location, known timeline, involved entities, witness names, available records, evidence at risk, and any attorney or insurer contacts. Avoid sending medical records, graphic material, account credentials, or other sensitive evidence through an unsecured first message. Request a confidential consultation to discuss lawful scope, jurisdiction, urgent preservation needs, budget, and reporting.
